question:
(a) Explain the role of work function and threshold frequency in photoelectric emission from a metal surface.
(b) In a photoelectric experiment, a metal of work function $2.4\,\text{eV}$ is illuminated by radiation of photon energy $3.6\,\text{eV}$. Find the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons and the stopping potential.

options.A:
(a) Work function is the energy released when an electron leaves the metal.
(b) $K_{\max}=6.0\,\text{eV}$ and $V_0=6.0\,\text{V}$.
options.B:
(a) Threshold frequency is independent of work function.
(b) $K_{\max}=2.4\,\text{eV}$ and $V_0=2.4\,\text{V}$.
options.D:
(a) Work function $\phi_0$ is the minimum escape energy; emission requires $h\nu\geq\phi_0$, and $\phi_0=h\nu_0$ at threshold.
(b) $K_{\max}=3.6-2.4=1.2\,\text{eV}$ and $V_0=1.2\,\text{V}$.
